cells.remarks: Gives the ancestry of the chief for six genera- tions. Records the gift, by the chief, of the income from certain lands in the village Kuduingabayu included in the Kudingali-grāma-rājya-pālu in the bima called Tribhuvanabhūshana in Bidure. Records also a gift by the chief of a silver cup and of money for the provision of rice-offering to god Chandra- prabhādēva in the same basti in the name of Vīramamma, the wife of his uncle Timmia- rasa. Refers also to a gift of money for the milk-bath of the deity in the name of Timmappa, son of Ghaṇṭōdeya.

cells.king: Vīrabhadra-Nāyaka ruling the Maṅgalūru and Bārākūru king-dom.
cells.date: Śaka 1562, Vikrama, Mārg aśira, ba. 2, Friday.
cells.remarks: Records a gift of money to reclaim a land at Paḍukōḍu in Peraṇḍa-māgaṇe which had been abandoned by the priests and for worship in the basti of Chandranātha-svāmi at Mūḍabidure, by Timmanaraśa alias Achela, as the land had become fallow after some time and consequently worship in the basti had stopped. Records the mortgage of his lands for 15 years by Mañjiśeṭṭi of Pējara to the Śantinātha-svāmi basti of Bidure for 200 earhās of gold received by him from the treasury of the basti of Chandrōgra Pārśvadēva at the instance of (the pontiff) Abhinava-Chārukīrtti Paṇḍitadēva. Records a gift of land to the Kallu-basti of Chandranātha-svāmi at Mūḍabidure by Sātabeḷe-Baḷḷāḷa of Marōvōḍi-grāma in Kōḍa-māgaṇe, a subdivision of Achela-sīme. The land was entrusted to a lady by name Chandraraṇi-avva Biyyāṇi for performing the Śalākāha-nōhi (festival) in the basti.

cells.remarks: Records the grant of the village Kōṇaki in Palli-rāshṭra by Vishnuvardhana-Mahārāja, son of Indravarama-Mahārāja, the younger brother of the ruling king, on the occasion of the lunar eclipse in the month of Kartika. The village was divided into 120 shares and allotted to several Brāhmaṇas in specified proportion. Refers to a previous donee of part of the village by name Viḍu-Śarmā of Añkūru, the ancestors of whom are stated to have been known as Ādytikāla-Varanaruchi on account of his great scholarship.

cells.remarks: Registers the grant of the village Neduri-garāya in Muṇḍarāshtra, by Yuvarāja-hārāja Vishṇugōpavarmaṇ, the son of Skandavarmaṇ, the grandson of Vīra-skandavarmaṇ, the great-grandson of Skandavarmaṇ of the Bhāradvāja-gōtra, to the three donees Doḍḍisvāmin, Kanna-svāmin and Nandisvāmin, of whom the first is given half the share, the second two-and-the third one-fourth, and the third part of the village which was converted into a Śaraṇika, rāma (asylum) and was exempted from the 18 kinds of impositions (?), the dēvabhōga lands in it being set apart... The grant was ordered to be maintained by the state officers such as the ayutakatas, niyōgikas, rājavallabhas etc. (Edited in the Telugu Journal, Bhāratī Vol. XVIII part I, pp. 699 ff.)

cells.remarks: Records that Pedaḍa Hobala Reddi, administering the six samājas under Mahāmaṇḍalēśvara Mahā-Maṇḍalēśvara Salva Timmarasa-vāru ruling from Peṇugoṇḍa, having undertaken to go on a pilgrimage to Ahōbilaṁ to fulfil a vow made by his forefathers, was instructed by the god, in a dream, to consecrate there a samprasi at Sāṁḍilya-kshētra near Sōmaghaṭṭa, where in (the god) would appear as Madhugiri Lakshmī-Narasiṁha, and that having constructed the temple accordingly, he secured the village Kauṇirūli-sīma into Gōraṁṭa-samutu to the god and also arranged for endowments for an archaka to conduct worship of the god.

cells.place: Slab set up on the tank bund.
cells.date: Śaka 1710, Saumya, Māgha, ba. 5, Fri- day, Hasati.
cells.remarks: States that Appāredḍi-Gaṁgireḍḍi, Peda-Pōlēreḍḍi, Vengal- reḍḍi, son of Gaṁgireddi, and others of Pichhāyi-chā- reḍḍi Nārāyaṇamma, having decided to construct a tank across the Tummalayēru at Rāchāyāpalle, Aḍūri Pāpiredḍi, the Reddi and Sambareḍdi Rāmachandrudu and others, at the time of settling the village under the name of Kālapalle government (drēgamarēvu), constructed the tank, established an agrahāra on śu. 15 in Māgha in the year Ānanda, on the occasion of a lunar eclipse, and settled in it Brāhmaṇas of the three sects holding 10 shares and 4 shares in all. The details of the taxes levied on lands cultivated under the tank, the mānyas given to the bōyas who constructed the tank and to the others who were entrusted with its upkeep.

cells.location: TIRUKKOYILUR TALUK
cells.place: contd. Tirumānallūr—contd. Same wall
cells.remarks: States that the temple of Toṇḍagal-Nayiṇār at Tirumānallūr, an independent village in the Tirukkōyilūr taluk, had become desolate for some years with the maṇḍapas and gōpuras fallen and that Amaramārār, the avasaram officer of the king, repaired them and after rehabilitating the village, made a gift of certain taxes accruing from the village for worship and offerings in the temple by order of the king. (See A.E. Nos. 111 and 213 of 1934-35). The order regarding this gift was communicated to the trustees of the temple.

cells.date: Śaka 1459(?), Man-matha, Dhanus, śu. [8] Thursday, Uttarāyādi.
cells.remarks: Stones lost in the middle. Seems to record the assignment of the income of 50 pon due from the village Mēttu-Urattūr as umbali-pon to Pāppārai and seven others for carrying the development of the temple of the god Śōkiśvaramuḍaiya-nāyinār at Tirunavālūr. Also records a gift of land in Mēttu-Urattūr by the beneficiaries to Meñhāna-mānuni, the disciple of Šikāļivajjal-Paydāram, for the benefit of the matha at Tirunavālūr. Mentions Sāļakarāja Tirumaladēva-Mahārāya and Tirumalarāja Bhōgaluyar belonging to the family of Uṟaiyūr Chōļas.

cells.date: 31st year (in words), Kumbha 26, śu. 1, Friday, Puraṭṭādi.
cells.remarks: Records an order of the king issued from his office room (ḍiḷḷu-maṇḍapa) at Varaṭṭai-pūrai [dēvaṉallūr in Āriya-nāḍu granting the village Toṇḍaikuḷam for the expenses of the worship, the celebration of the daily services in the temple, of festivals and of the sacred bath on ash-days in the daśak fortnight. Puraṭṭādi is stated to be the birth-star of the king. Refers to some previous gifts made by the king in the 21st year to the temple of Tiruppagavā-pūrai-Pāṇḍyadēva. Refors also to a donation made for conducting during the Paṅguṇi-uttiram festival.]

cells.place:
East wall of the mandapa in front of the
central shrine in the Kailasanätha
temple.
cells.remarks: Records an agreement by the Sivabrāhmaṇas of the temple of Kailasam-Udāyār at Ten-Tiruppai-dita-Samudrappaty, born of the cervant-maids of the temple, to supply two measures of twelve lamps daily from before the deity for the money received by them from Ilambaruttuppillai, another Sivabrāhmaṇa of the same temple. Above this inscription is a fragmentary record dated in the 3rd year and 8th day of [a year] whose name is lost, confirming some endowment by the king made by his predecessor (Sivabhūdar) for the worship of goddess Tirukkāmakōṭṭu-Āluḍaiya-Nāchchiyar consecrated in the temple by the descendant of the above Sivabrāhmaṇas of the temple. The paddy was alloted by the Sivabrāhmaṇas to one Andär Ponnārmēniyār for the worship of Gaṇapati probably within the same temple.

cells.place: Slab lying near the ruined temple of Śiva.
cells.remarks: Registers gift of land made by Narsākaḍga, son of Tiru- malarājayya, grandson and grandson of king Timmarāja for the benefit of the god Chennakēśava st... ... on the bank of the Kumudvatī in the Chêngalamari-sīma of Muliki-nāḍu in the Udayagiri-rājya. The donor bears a number of epithets, such as Boyiddakapurvarāja, Madhvarājava-pradishṭa, Baṇḍeyakolāpakāleya, āchārya, etc. He belonged to the solar race and Vaśishṭha- gōtra and is said to be a subordinate of the king. Also records a provision made to the pipers, etc., for service in the temple.

Records a sale of land by the sabhā of Kunrattūr alias Mārlīmahākāla-chaturvēdimangalam in Mugai-nāḍu, a subdivision of Palkunrak-kōṭṭam, to a member of the dēvaṅgaṇa of the village. Another fragmentary inscription in the same place beginning with the same introduction records a sale of land by the same sabhā to a member of the village-assembly of Dēndēśvaramuttan, who evidently assigned it for lamps during the three sandis in the temple of Daṇḍēśvara constructed by him. A third fragmentary inscription of the king engraved close by and beginning with the same introduction is dated in the 19th year.

cells.king: Achyutarāya-Mahārāya, son of Narasāradēva Mahārāya ' who was pleased to take all countries '.
cells.remarks: Beginning lost. States that the mahā-mandapa and ardha-mandapa, evidently of the temple, got Tiruvik-vachchhirupākkattadēva at Korramangalam was constructed of stone and also that a stone image of Rishabhadeva was set up by Attimala (Hastimalai) aliza Kannaradēva Prithivigangādaraiyan, chief of Pādā-nādu, and another for pūr-maryādā and that he gave the village Korramangalam for providing offerings to the deity and for feeding daily eight Brāhmaṇas. A portion of the historical introduction of Rājarāja begins with the words 'Tirumagalpola etc., is found closely below. Another inscription in the same place states that Perumāmanadigal wishing to respect the gift of Prithivigangaraiyan issued an order to this effect through his adhikāri Mugaiyuruiyān and Minavan Muvendavēļān.

cells.remarks: The gōpura of the Jain temple was constructed with the stones from the ruined Śiva temple on the hillock. Some of the inscribed stones are missing. Seems to record the decision regarding the right of collecting grain-fees granted by certain villages to the temple of Ammaiarraiya-Nāyār Marudarāsar-Padaivīdu with the right of collecting a small cess (alku) in them. Also states that these communities bestowed upon Iruvēngalanāthar, son of Mala-Appana-yakkar, the title 'Marainpulak-kāvalan'.

cells.place: Stone planted in the Minākshi-Nāyaka maṇḍapa.
cells.remarks: Records the provision made for daily worship in the Śrī Minākshi-Sōmasundarēśvara temple from the interest on one lakh of pagodas endowed by Pachchiappan Pachchayappa Mudaliyār. Also provides for the appointment of a tutor on 10 varāhas for a month for teaching law (vivakāra-śāstra) and another on 5 varāhas for teaching English to Hindu boys of the locality. (See also No. 145 of 1938–39).

cells.place:
Sidhēśvaram.–Two sides of a pillar
built into the platform of the dastur-
khāna.
cells.date:
Śaka, [983] Plava,
Jyēshṭha, Amāvā-
syā, Wednesday,
solar eclipse.
cells.remarks: Damaged. Mentions the Telugu Chola chief Irugapachāria Mahārāja who was governing Sindavadi-1000, Periakel-800, and was granted the agrahāra of Mosalayamaduvu and and another 1,500 vars. Ayyadevarasa, son of Mosalayamaduvu and records a gift of the toll-incomes of the river at Sidhēśvara to the disciple (name not clear) of the ascetic Kalyāna- śakti who was the sthānādhipati of Sidhēśvara.

cells.king:
Mahāmaṇdalēśvara Gaṇapatidēva
Mahārāja, ruling from Orugallu.
cells.remarks: Registers a gift of some vrittis of land to two villages made by Mattala Mallayya, a feudatory of the king to god Viśva- nāthu at Sidhēśvara whose temple was constructed by Gana- padēva-Samanta, overseer of the prākāra of the temple of Gana- padēva Mahārāja. The management of the endowed land was handed over to Pōchūriju Vengana Pegada, the agent of Vidyāśirāvaleya, who was the sthānapati of Saṁgamēśvara and Bhāśārakshētra.

cells.king: Dēvarāya Mahārāya, ‘who was pleased to witness the elephant hunt’.
cells.date: Śaka 1557, Yuva, Vṛiśhika, ba. 7, Makhā, Friday.
cells.remarks: Records the remission of water-cess (nīr-vilai) of 5 pon in 1330 of land granted for providing offerings on the day of the god Veḷḷāṅgāṭṭīśvara-nāyaṇār of the village of Pōḷiyūr in Siruvāḷ-nāḍu on the north bank of the river Śēyāru and granted to the temple of Varadarāja-Perumāḷ at Kāñchīpuram. The land was later resumed but the possession was resumed from the temple and settlement in it encouraged by promising not to levy taxes for five years.

cells.place: Two stones set up by the side of the Śiva temple in ruins.
cells.date: Śaka 1432, Kīlaka, Mīna, śu. 10, Sunday, Mūla.
cells.remarks: Much damaged. Records that Śiva-Dīkshita, son of Malla-māṁba, who was learned and had performed many māthas, obtained the village Kiñjikuppam from the king and after constructing two tanks, gave it to four of his relatives who were instructed that they should be pious, should not bear any ill-will amongst themselves, nor mingle with people with other castes, should be ardent in the study of the Vēdas and Śāstras and should worship only gods like Vishnu or Īśvara and not evil deities.

cells.remarks: Records the endowment, to please god Madukanātha, of the village Kakukani by the chief Karuvūra Sānta- Dannāyaka and the several gaudas of the Kabunaligeya- sime. Further, on the occasion of a solar eclipse, Kampana into the lands of Simana Midappa who was entrusted it from him. Siriyana Midappa who was entrusted with the endowment it bestowed on the learned Brāhmaṇas living in the śarkanmas and the śēstras dividing the same into twelve shares. It registers a grant called Lakshmi- puran, on Magha ba. 30 of the same year.

cells.place:

entrance of the rangamantapa of the
Mahābbalēśvara temple.
cells.remarks: Records a gift of land for the maintenance of a satra in the the temple of the god Mahābala of Gōkarna when Mahāpradhāna Bankarasa-Vodeya's son (name lost) was governing the province of 'Hayive, Tulu and Konkana from his capital at Honnavara. cells.remarks: Partly damaged. cells.place: Slab set up near the Miru-Kalasada guḍi
cells.date: Cāḷukya-Vikrama-kāla 45, Subhakṛt, Pushya, ba. 13, Sunday. Uttarāyaṇasankrānti.
cells.remarks: Damaged. Commences with the praise of the gods Tri- kajēśvara and Gangēśvara. Registers an endowment of land including wet lands for the feeding and clothing of the ascetics living in the maṭha attached to it by the Thirty Representatives (mūvadimbaru) of Sōval. The gift was made into the hands of Kaliyuga-siddha Abhinava-vādīndra. It mentions that the Gangēśvara was built after the consecration of the god Gangēśvara by Gangārāśi.

cells.remarks: In characters of about the 14th century A.D. Mentions the Śaka year 31 (current) Śubhakṛt, and states that the Cāḷukyas (Cāḷukya-Satyāśrayadēva and states that the grants were made to the twenty grahāras of Modallūr by Honnakomtada Mīleya. cells.location: Bījūr
cells.place: Slab standing near Basavaṇṇa- dēvara Guḍi.
cells.date: Śaka 1168, Vāva. vasu, Pushya, ba. Amāvāsye, Monday, solar eclipse.
cells.remarks: Damaged and worn out. Registers gifts of house-site, oil-mill, other rituals, feeding the Brahmins, etc., in the three temples of Basavaṇṇa, etc., at Bījūr. Registers gifts of land and money by Vinchuva Basavarasas of the Gautama-gōtra for the merit of the deceased Bhāgabayi(y). Basavarasa was Bāhataraṇiyōgādhipati and Sarādhikāri to Vāsudēva Bhaṭṭōpādhyāya who was the governor of the districts of Tarda- Kāṇambade and Tarddavāḍi from Vijayapura. Bījūr [Bīlava] was situated in the Kaṇambade-nāḍu, included in [Karahāṭa]- which formed a part of Kuntala-vishaya.

cells.place: Another slab standing in the same place.
cells.date: Śaka 1168, Vāva. vasu, Pushya, ba. Amāvāsye, Monday, solar eclipse.
cells.remarks: Damaged and worn out. Registers gifts of house-site, oil mill, wet lands, etc., for the daily worship of the god Basavēśvara whose temple was constructed at Bījūr by Vinchuva Basa- varasa of the Gautama-gōtra. Bījūr was situated in the Kaṇambade-nāḍu included in the Karahāṭa-dēśa which formed a part of Kuntala-vishaya. Basavarasa was the sarvādh- kāri of Vēsugudēva son of Bhāgabāyi and his minister Kam- naya. The gifts were made while governing the districts of Tarda- vāḍi and Heda Kaṇambade from their headquarters at Vijaya pura as subordinates of the king.

cells.location: Guḍḍāpūr
cells.place: Slab set up in the Dānamma's temple.
cells.date: 4th year, Parābhava, Pushya, śu. 14, Monday, [Uttara]- Rēvaya. Amāvāsye.
cells.remarks: Damaged and worn out. Registers a gift of land for the benefit of the god Vīra-Sōmanātha of the village Sōradi for the benefit of the god Guḍḍīpe-priya Svayambhu-Sōma- nātha, by the king and his officer Mahāpradhāna Sēnādhi- pati Vīra-Gōyidēva-Daṇḍanāyaka. The temple was built from their camp at Hū-Bannūru. The gift was made into the hands of Vīrabhaṭṭi-kāśēvarasamyāsi Sakaiya Taileyagalu. Some other gifts of land into his hands are also registered.

cells.location: Umarāṇi
cells.place: Slab set up at the right wall in the Hēmāḷinga temple.
cells.date: Śaka 1089 (in words), Sarvajit, Vaiśākha, Amāvāsye, Monday, solar eclipse.
cells.remarks: Damaged. Registers a gift of land and oil-mill for the benefit of the Hēmāḷinga Mahādēva at Umarāṇi by the Gāvuṇḍas, Dēviga-ḍa, Maduvanayya and other Karaṇas at the instance of the king. This Hēmāḷi bore the title Kopana-puravarādhīś- vara. Also mentions the chief of Uṇḍaravāḍi (modern Umarāṇi), the chief town of the thirty-two villages of the Heda-Kalamba- baḍe-nāḍu, which was included in Karahāḍa Four-Thou- sand province of the Kuntala-dēśa. Also states that Madu- vanayya Daṇḍanāyaka and Malliḍēva-Daṇḍanāyaka were governing the province of Heḍa-Kalambaḍe-nāḍu.

cells.remarks: Registers a gift of land for a charity pickota at Valasaṅga by Sāvanta Haḍḍarasa and the headman Chauḍamayya, when Mahāmaṇḍaleśvara Gōbhāṇarasa was governing the province of Karahāḍa Four-Thousand and his grandmother Abhinava-Chaṇḍadēvī was administering Valasaṅga, situated in Kaḷambade Three-Hundred division. The last named is described as Abhinava-Sāradādēvī as the wife of Tribhuvanamalla-dēva (Vikramāditya VI).

cells.remarks: Issued from Śāntanapura. States that the Mahārāṇaka with the permission of Ananta-Mahādevī, the chief queen (of the king) granted to the Brāhmaṇa Śūmasvāmin of the Kauṇḍinya gotra, land in the city of Ambrakannagara. The king Harijña is stated to be the son of Mahārājādhirāja and grandson of [Bha]- grahaja of the Śūra-vaṃśa. The record is in characters of about the 5-6th centuries A.D. Published in J.U.P.I.S., Vol. XVIII, p. 167.

cells.remarks: Gives the Western Gaṅga genealogy. Reco-ds the gift of four khaṇḍukas of land in the village of Sirandarangalampalau situated in Pudukanḍa-viṣaya to a Brāhmaṇa named Nīlakaṇṭha Śarman, the last of the five sons of Nīlakaṇṭha of the Harita-gotra, probably by Dugganāmā, the king's son, at the request of his wife Kancikāmbā. Gives also the genealogy of Nīlakaṇ- ṭha, the wife of Dugganāmā, and the older sister (?) of Indrarāja, whose descent for three generations is traced from a king called Nīlamappa. [Published in Ep. Ind., Vol. XXVII, pp. 145 ff.

cells.remarks: Published in I.H.Q., Vol. XX, pp. 245 ff. The record is issued by the king from his victorious camp at Suvarṇapura. Regis- ters the gift, by the king, of the village of Kāliṇḍā in Tikkārikā-viṣaya in Kōsala- dēśa to Kālaśadēva Bhaṭṭa, Bhaṭṭaputra, who was a vādhyāya (resident) of Saṇḍakāpaka and was the son of Gāṅgēya and grandson of Arjuna. The donee is stated to have hailed from Muktāvatī in Śrāvastī. The record also states that the donee was it- suided at Āhjjigrāma.

cells.place: Another slab in the same place.
cells.remarks: In characters of about the 16th century A. D. States that the 360-Ekaiṁvīras, the devotees of the goddess Chau- dēśvarī, and Paṇṭi-mūrti-Nāyaka, son of Mahamaṇḍalēś vara Vīrupārāya-ayyadēva Mahārāja, the ruler of Paṇu- gallu, in order to relieve the siege laid to his fort by a certain Gururāja of Nandahāram, came out victorious and were conferred several titles by the chief in apprecia- tion of their success and bravery, and records an endow- ment made by them (the Ekāṅgavīras) at one ruuñka per head to the goddess.

cells.place: South wall of the same temple.
cells.king: Tribh. Kulōttuṅga-Chōḷadēva "who was pleased to take Madura and the crowned head of the Pāṇḍya."
cells.remarks: States that the 'Padineṇbhūmi-viśaiya-nagaraṭṭār' including those of Vīraśōlanallūr and Āraḷūr met in the Daṇṇadi-vajan-tirukkāvanam in the temple of Śrī-Kailāsamuḍaiya-Nāyaṇār at Urattūr and made provision for maintaining 27 lamps of Tiruvālīśvaram and 145 on annual festival days in the temple of Tiruvālīśvaram. Vāḷikāṇḍapuram was made claimed as their nagarakkāni. Vāḷikāṇḍapuram was made into a Sāraḍāfam(?) i.e., military quarter(?) and provision was also made for repairing the car (belonging to the temple) from the income of the village and the amañji due to the (officer) Vāṇavadaraiya.

cells.remarks: States that Raghunōji-Paṇḍitarāyan exempted the new settlers in the town of Chidambaram from the payment of taxes like aḍippu-vari and sungān-vari on the repree-sentations made by Nāyakkāṭi-Nāṭṭār and the piramāyappillai. cells.date: Śaka 1299, Plavaṅga, Jyēshṭha ba. 1, Sunday-A. D. 1377, May 24, Sunday.
cells.remarks: Records the construction of a bell-tower, doors etc., to the central shrine of god Agastyēśvara formerly built by Pillalamarri Bēti-Reḍḍi and the gift of vessels, cloth, etc., to the god by Kadiyamu Pōtināyuḍu, the servant of the king, for the religious merit of his master Ana-Vēmaya Reḍḍi. cells.place: Slab in the Vīrabhadra temple in the fort.
cells.king: Ana-Vēmaya Reḍḍi, son of Vēma Reḍḍi
cells.date: Śaka 1522, Vikāri, Kārttika ba. di. 13, Monday, November 5, Monday, 1599.
cells.remarks: Records the gift of vartanas by the Viśvabrahmās of all countries to god Śrīṅgāra Vīrabhadra. It was accordingly declared that the devotees need not pay the vartanas to the Kammaṭas, but should pay them to the god. Similarly the Tammalas, Bāṭīju, Gauḍas and others are accountable to the god. Mentions Mahāmaṇḍala Khulli Bādāśa.

cells.king: Ana-Vēmaya Reḍḍi, son of Vēma Reḍḍi
cells.date: Śaka 1528, Plavaṅga, Phālguṇa, ba. 5, Thursday, A.D. 1608, February 25, Thursday. (The Śaka year is wrong for 1608)
cells.remarks: Records that the Bhaṭṭu hailing from the times of Dēvarakoṇḍa, Koṇḍavīḍu, Nallagoṇḍa, Uṇḍragoṇḍa, Koṇḍapalli, Oṅgōlu, Amarāvati, Bellakoṇḍa, Vinikoṇḍa, Nāgārjunakoṇḍa, Taṅgēḍa, Gurijāla, Kāramapūṇḍi, Tuma-kūru, etc., who had come to Vōḍapalli, for the marriages of the Kōmaṭi made a permanent endowment of a portion of their incomes (pāyaka-pāyida) to god Narasiṁha at the temple of Vōḍapalli. Similarly the Kōmaṭis also agreed to pay to the god a sum of one māḍa and 1 śāṇa of rice on the occasion of each marriage.

cells.place: Third slab at the same place
cells.king: Mahāmaṇḍa Pāḍuśā, son of Hajarati Pāḍuśā Yihkunda-hinu ruling at Golkonda.
cells.date: Śaka 1530, Kīlaka, Jyēshṭha, ba. 3, Sunday-A. D. 1608 May 22, Sunday; .53
cells.remarks: Records that the village of Krottapalli was granted as dēvadāya agrahāra to god Narasiṁhavāmin for providing daily offerings and worship and for maintaining a Rāmānuja-kūṭam by Talapāṇṭuri Kōnappa, who was the head of administration under Mālik Amīr-ul-Mulk to whom the Pāḍuśā had granted the village at the time of his visit to Vājirābād as mokhāsa. The donor is stated to have made the gift on the request of Chintā-Reḍḍi, Basvi-Reḍḍi, Doḍḍa Mēdhava Rao and several others who were the samastavāru of Sāagōji Boppa-Dēvuḷagāru.

cells.remarks: Refers to the restoration of former grant to Rudraśakti- Paṇḍita by Mahāmaṇḍalēśvara Āvanigada Vikrama- dityadēva. Also records that the king, at the request of Ballināyya, Tikkapayya and others headed by Vikramāditya, made some grants of land to the god Vikramēśvara. cells.date: Year..., Subhānu, Āshāḍa-hēḍyudvāchchhiṭāshṭīye, Thurs-day, solar eclipse.
cells.remarks: Mutilated and worn out. States that while senādhipati Pirayas [aṇa]ramma [Bānu]gi-500 and Haṇikkure-300 in, along with the prabhu-kāruṇīka of Haṇungal-500, renewed the gift formerly made by Mahāmaṇḍalēśvara [Taila] bha of the village of Haṇungal-500. The gift was made into the hands of Tribhuvanasakti-Paṇḍita who was in charge of the temple of god Svayambhū-Kāḷidēva of Paṇhiḷagere. Also registers a gift of land made by the same prabhu of the village of Daṇṇāyaka Himmarnasabha into the purpose of the village of Haṇungal, in the presence of the Prathig[auuṇ]da of Koṇṭakuḷ-30, and with the consent of Gommanagauṇda.

cells.remarks: Damaged and worn out. Registers gift of land and oil for the daily worship, etc., in the temple of Svayambhū-Kāḷidēvasvāmin of god Nāchēśvara by Perggade Narasinga, when Tailapa was governing Banavāsi-12,000 and Pānuṁgal-500. The gift was made into the hands of Rudraśakti-Paṇḍita, the disciple of Kuyyēra-Māmbhaṭṭa. It also registers other gifts by the village of Vaḷḷavāḍa and the sarvakarayagade Bammadēva of Hoṭṭiyūr and others.

cells.date:
(i) Śaka 1098, Jaya, Jyēshṭha, amāvāsye, Sunday, solar eclipse, vyatīpāta.,
(ii) Śaka [1096], Jaya, Mārgasira, puṇṇami, Sunday, lunar eclipse.
(iii) Śaka 1098, Jaya, Mārgasira, ba. amāvāsye, Tuesday, solar eclipse.
cells.remarks: Registers several gifts by Daṇḍanāyaka Mahēśvara to the dēvagrāha Brahmasingi-Paṇḍita for the temple of god Svayambhū-Kallēśvara with the witness Vāsudēva-Daṇḍādhīpa, son of the king's subordinate, Kēsinayya, who was governing Pāṇungal-500. Also records on this day certain gifts for the same temple by the daṇḍanāyaka Vīra-Vāsudēva with Daṇḍanāyaka Māyidēvarasa, Mahāmāṇḍalēśvara Indrakarasa, and Sthānāpati Sānimayya. Registers some more gifts for the same temple and Brashmāsiṅgi-Paṇḍita by some others headed by Daṇḍanāyaka-māyidēvarasa who was in charge of the manne of Kāladi-86. Records the death of a hero in a fight.

Registers some gifts of land to the temple of Matikaṭṭi-bhaṭṭāraka by rēggaḍe Kālimayya for the merit of his father who constructed it and named it after him. The donor is described as the pāda-padmōpajīvin of the Trailōkya-malladēva, evidently of the Chālukya family.Read more (1 KB)

cells.location: Niralgi
cells.place: Slab set up in front of the temple of Vīrabhadradēva.
cells.date: Chālukya Vikrama year.... Viśvāvasu, Akshaya tritiyā, māvase, Monday, solar eclipse, vyatīpāta.
cells.remarks: Registers some gifts of land by Kasi [chya] na-bhaṭṭōpādhyāya for the perpetual lamp, oblations, etc., of the temple of god Kālidēvasvāmi, when [Tai] laha was governing Pānuṅgal-500. It also records that the gift was made to Rudraśakti-paṇḍita. It also records some more gifts to the same temple by the aivattokkalu and the nakhara, etc.
